views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the current posture and let the May 19 trade framework execute rather than escalating or conceding. Keep the tariff threat (up to $150B, first $50B) in reserve as leverage while China works through its purchase commitments, and press the structural IP/forced-technology-transfer issues in the follow-up Beijing talks without reigniting the trade war or undercutting the ZTE penalty without adequate concession.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to US interests has fallen sharply from the April peak. The May 19 joint statement delivered a major US win — China agreed to 'significantly increase' purchases of US goods and services, and both sides put the threatened tariffs 'on hold' (Mnuchin: 'we're putting the trade war on hold'; Politico/CNN/LA Times, 2018-05-20). The US retains all leverage: Lighthizer explicitly warned tariffs, investment restrictions and export controls remain available if China fails to deliver, and Kudlow said tariffs 'have to be part of any enforcement.' Macro shows the dispute has not yet bitten the US economy — industrial production ~102.4 and rising, consumer sentiment ~98, the broad dollar index firm near 111.7, 10Y near 3.0%, WTI ~$71 (country_health). That combination — leverage plus an economy that is still strong — reads as an opportunity (-0.4 on the US anchor: extract concessions, onshore/technology posture, political upside from being tough) rather than a threat. On action, escalation would be imprudent now: the truce is working, markets rallied, and Congress is already pushing back domestically on overreaching (bipartisan Senate rebuke over softening ZTE penalties); full concession would be premature since the statement is intentionally vague with no dollar figure and structural IP issues unresolved (Schumer and CSIS's Kennedy both noted it commits neither side to specific action). The correct move is to hold, keep the tariff club visible, and hold China to execution — eschewing both escalation that could blow up the cease-fire and concession that would squander newly won leverage.
key_factors: May 19 joint statement: China pledges to 'significantly increase' US purchases; tariffs put on hold
US retains tariff leverage (up to $150B, first $50B) in reserve; Lighthizer/Kudlow keep enforcement tools available
No real-economy damage yet: IP ~102.4 rising, sentiment ~98, dollar firm ~111.7, oil ~$71
Statement deliberately vague — no dollar figure, structural IP/forced-tech-transfer issues unresolved
Congressional pushback against softening ZTE penalties signals domestic constraint on escalation
Deal framework fragile; economies warn of 'periodic ceasefires' and possible resumption of tensions

US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown.
